Note::NlpAccessor::remove_brackets¶

Back to Note NLP Accessor API Reference

Signature¶

Note Note::NlpAccessor::remove_brackets() const

Remove Balanced Bracketed Asides With Their Contents¶

remove_brackets() deletes balanced spans delimited by parentheses (), square brackets [], or braces {}. Both delimiters and everything between them disappear. Use it when bracketed material is ancillary to the surrounding text, such as editorial notes, compact metadata, or inline alternatives. It is not the right operation when only the delimiter characters should be removed while their contents remain.

Each delimiter family supports nesting of its own kind. A balanced outer span also removes any differently bracketed text inside it because that text is part of the outer span. The families are processed as parentheses, then square brackets, then braces; surviving text retains its original order.

Malformed delimiters are handled conservatively:

Input condition

Result

Balanced opening and closing delimiter

Entire span is deleted.

Opening delimiter with no matching close

Opening delimiter and following text are retained.

Closing delimiter with no preceding open

Closing delimiter is retained.

Nested balanced spans of the same family

Removed as one outer span.

This policy prevents a truncated document from losing its entire suffix merely because it contains an unmatched opening bracket.

After at least one balanced span is removed, ASCII whitespace in the cell is collapsed and stripped. Punctuation outside the span is not repaired, so a space before a surviving semicolon can remain. If no balanced span exists, the cell is returned byte-for-byte. The operation is shape-preserving, out-of-place, and limited to Text Notes; empty and undefined inputs follow the shared transformation contract.

Example 1: Balanced Spans And Mixed Delimiters¶

std::cout << pluss::note::print(
    pluss::note::make({
        "Keep (draft [old]) final {meta}; literal unmatched (kept"})
        .nlp().remove_brackets()) << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[1], dim=1, numel=1, encoding=utf8)
["Keep final ; literal unmatched (kept"]

The square brackets vanish with the balanced outer parentheses. The final unmatched opening parenthesis and its text survive.

Example 2: Same-Family Nesting And An Unmatched Close¶

std::cout << pluss::note::print(
    pluss::note::make({"Nested [one [two] three] end; closing ] stays"})
        .nlp().remove_brackets()) << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[1], dim=1, numel=1, encoding=utf8)
["Nested end; closing ] stays"]

Example 3: Malformed-Only Input Is A True No-Op¶

std::cout << pluss::note::print(
    pluss::note::make({"  unmatched ( text  "})
        .nlp().remove_brackets()) << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[1], dim=1, numel=1, encoding=utf8)
["  unmatched ( text  "]

Example 4: Apply Independently Across A Matrix¶

const auto matrix = pluss::note::make(
    std::vector<std::string>{"Copyright 2026", "a (draft)",
                             "- item", "use `x` now"},
    std::array<std::int64_t, 2>{2, 2});
std::cout << pluss::note::print(
    matrix.nlp().remove_brackets()) << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[2, 2], dim=2, numel=4, encoding=utf8)
[
  ["Copyright 2026", "a"], 
  ["- item", "use `x` now"]
]

Failure And Absence¶

An empty Text Note returns an empty Note with the same extents. Undefined propagates. Bytes, Bool, Int64, and Float64 Notes throw pluss::Error; the method does not decode arbitrary bytes or format typed values as text first.
